pass: The post-1850 economic boom in the United States had its greatest impact on eastern mill towns, such as Lowell, Massachusetts. Formerly peaceful villages became bustling towns whose factories rose to dominate their skylines. Their populations sometimes tripled in a decade, forcing propertyless workers into overcrowded, dilapidated housing. Their economies came under the domination of industrialists who competed unfairly with one another and were contemptuous of the old ways. These industrialists had economic power and the social and political power that accompanied it; town politicians catered to their interests. Other property owners, especially small-business entrepreneurs and professionals, identified with them and applauded their successes. The factory workers inevitably found themselves alienated from property owners and helpless before their employers. Thus, economic class, social status, and power were inextricably intertwined; control over property and machinery was readily transformed into complete authority.

Upon impact, the asteroid vaporizes both itself and the target rock, producing a vapor plume that condenses into spherules. These form a layer preserved in rock, whose age can be estimated using radiometric dating. Scientists know of fourteen of these spherule ____ layers scattered across Earth, but none dates to the theorized lunar cataclysm time period. Four layers, however, are from between 3.47 and 3.24 billion years ago, indicating perhaps a slow decline in collisions.
